extracted_factors.Label: Economic Benefits of Agriculture
extracted_factors.Description: Areas with favorable conditions for agriculture or proximity to markets encourage deforestation as they offer higher economic returns compared to forests.
extracted_factors.Tags: Agriculture, Economic Returns, Market Proximity, Deforestation

extracted_factors.Label: Global Market Demand
extracted_factors.Description: Global market demand for agricultural products can incentivize deforestation through price increases, indirectly encouraging land conversion from forest to agriculture.

extracted_factors.Label: Protected Areas and Law Enforcement
extracted_factors.Description: The establishment of protected areas and enforcement of forest laws are policies that directly contribute to reduced deforestation by restricting land use conversion.

extracted_factors.Label: Presence of Roads and Infrastructure
extracted_factors.Description: Proximity to roads and infrastructure lowers transportation costs, making remote forest areas more accessible and increasing deforestation rates.

extracted_factors.Label: Payments for Ecosystem Services (PES)
extracted_factors.Description: PES programs provide incentives for preserving forests, although effectiveness depends on proper targeting of areas under threat of deforestation.

extracted_factors.Label: Population Growth
extracted_factors.Description: Increasing population pressures result in higher demand for land and resources, driving deforestation as more land is converted for human use.

extracted_factors.Label: Indigenous Land Management
extracted_factors.Description: Lands managed by indigenous communities are often associated with lower deforestation rates due to better sustainable practices and legal recognition.

extracted_factors.Label: Higher Elevation and Steeper Slopes
extracted_factors.Description: These geographical features make deforestation more difficult and costly, resulting in lower deforestation rates.
